stem: During a school nature walk, Meera picks up a fallen mango leaf and observes that its veins spread out from a thick middle vein and join again to form a net-like pattern on both sides of the leaf. Which type of venation does the mango leaf show?

options.text: Parallel venation, because the veins run side by side
Reticulate venation, because the veins form a net-like pattern
Parallel venation, because the veins join again at the tip
Reticulate venation, because the leaf has a thick middle vein only

teacher.key_rationale: A net-like (web) pattern of veins branching from a midrib is reticulate venation, typical of dicot leaves such as mango. Options A and C incorrectly classify the leaf as parallel venation; D cites the midrib alone, which does not define the venation type.
